Eleven comments

Paddy Fahey’s other hornpipe

Another Paddy Fahey tune and I think its a great one! I first heard this hornpipe from Anne Conroy Burke over a year ago at a class in the Joe Mooney Summer School. I joined her class mid week and this had been done earlier so all I had was a tape recording from which I tried subsequently to learn the tune. I could never get past the first couple of bars and snatches of the tune elsewhere - it jumps around the place a bit and my inexperienced ear couldn’t keep up! Came across a transcription by Josephine Keegan lately, she has it in Bflat and the tune varies a little from Anne’s version. Anyway this helped me to get past the bits I was stuck on. This is Anne’s version in G - I’m not sure about the linking triplet, try a few and see what you like : Bcd doesn’t sound right to me. Also I think Anne plays the dcd triplet as a roll.

↳ Posted by Kilcash on August 23rd, 2005.

Paddy Fahey’s, X:4

Here’s a setting (as given in the appendix to the Maria Holohan Thesis) with accompanying chords. I suspect some will say that this shouldn’t be attempted, especially with Paddy Fahey’s tunes, but I did it anyway so, in the event of such objections, please feel free to ignore this posting.

I’ve notated all the PF tunes in that collection and added chord accomp., but won’t push my luck by posting any more of them - at least not for a while.

↳ Posted by Bazza on August 20th, 2020.

Re: Paddy Fahey’s

Bazza, I think it’s a great idea. It will help backers who are unfamiliar with the style and it gives insight into the melodies’ progression from a harmonic viewpoint. I think probably most, if not all, of Maria Holohan’s transcriptions have been posted as transcribed, so this is a welcome addition.

Thanks! I’d like to see more.

↳ Posted by Steve Owen on August 20th, 2020.

Paddy Fahey’s, X:5

Well, encouraged by comments such as the one above, I’ll carry on posting Paddy Fahey tunes with added chords. Here’s his hornpipe No 1 in G (or chords for 3rd fret capo if you’re playing in the original key of Bb).

The chord choices are mine and and I make no claims as to authenticity. Quite a lot of the PF tunes given in the Holohan collection can be tricky when it comes to pinning down harmonies, so if you don’t agree with the way I’ve done it - or think that any chordal accomp is out of place - then please change or disregard what I’ve attached to this one and others that I’ll submit.

↳ Posted by Bazza on August 21st, 2020.
